title: Security Analysis of LXoP for General Width
summary: The width-two LXoP security analysis is technically extendable to very small larger widths, but deriving an analysis for general width remains open.

formal_statement.body: For the construction $\mathrm{LXoP}[L,w,n]$, with an invertible linear function $L$ on $\{0,1\}^n$ satisfying $x \oplus L^j(x) \ne 0$ for every nonzero $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and $1 \le j \le w$, extend the existing security analysis of $\mathrm{LXoP}[L,2,n]$ to general $w > 2$. The extension is known to be technically feasible for very small values of $w > 2$, but deriving the security analysis for general $w$ remains unresolved.

scope.domain: Security analysis of the LXoP construction in symmetric cryptography.
assumptions: L is an invertible linear function on binary vectors of dimension n, and every nonzero x satisfies x XOR L iterated j times on x is nonzero for indices from 1 through w.
parameters: L: the linear-function parameter of LXoP
w: the parameter governing the target generalization and the range of iterate indices
n: the dimension of the binary-vector domain
scope.unresolved_remainder: Derive the security analysis of LXoP[L,w,n] for general w greater than two.

citations.label: Combining Outputs of a Random Permutation: New Constructions and Tight Security Bounds by Fourier Analysis

progress.summary: The source says extending the width-two analysis to very small widths above two is feasible but technical. It leaves the more involved analysis for general width to future work.
citation_labels: Itai Dinur et al., Combining Outputs of a Random Permutation: New Constructions and Tight Security Bounds by Fourier Analysis
